svg.font-family: Inter, 'Space Grotesk', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: A traffic jam re-routes Bologna to Roma about a millisecond after the commit
svg.desc: Map of central Italy. The fastest route from Bologna to Roma, 287 minutes, runs over the A1 through Prato and Firenze. A jam on the A1 between Bologna and Prato is written to the database with one UPDATE. The contraction hierarchy re-prices only the arcs above that road, in about a millisecond, and the next query returns the new fastest route through Forli, Arezzo and Perugia, 295 minutes.
svg.text: -- 4 hours of queue on the A1
Only the arcs above the jammed road are re-priced.
Queries never wait: meanwhile, Dijkstra answers.
Live traffic: one UPDATE, a new route a millisecond later
The C in CCH is for customizable: the hierarchy is kept, only the costs above a changed road are recomputed.
